title: Our species and our sourced variants mapped onto experimental interface positions
bird_exclusion: Class Aves is this project's frozen holdout; no bird sequence was aligned and no bird species is in the panel, until the holdout exam runs.

coordinate_mapping_method.step1: Interface positions come from the deposited coordinates in the structure's own reference-sequence numbering (SIFTS alignment, RCSB rcsb_polymer_entity_align).
coordinate_mapping_method.step2: Each panel species' UniProt sequence is aligned to that reference sequence with a global BLOSUM62 alignment (Bio.Align, blastp scoring, gap open -11, extend -1), and the interface position is read through that alignment.
uncertainty: A one-to-one alignment column is an assumption, not a measurement. Where the alignment places a gap, the position has no counterpart and is reported as a gap, not as a difference.

Identity between the structure's protein and each panel species is reported per species; below roughly 50% identity a single-residue correspondence should not be trusted, and the K2P and some transporter mappings are in that range.

The structures are human (and one mouse) proteins. Every position in a fish or insect protein is therefore reached by a cross-species jump, and paralogy (kcnk5a/kcnk5b, gja1a/gja1b, shha/shhb) can place the alignment on the wrong copy.

Interface membership is defined at a 4.0 A heavy-atom cutoff in one deposited conformation. A residue just outside the cutoff, or one that only contacts the partner in another state, is scored as non-interface here.

lat4_substrate_site_across_the_panel.ligand: PHE (a free phenylalanine bound in the substrate site)
lat4_substrate_site_across_the_panel.note: This is the experimental substrate site of OUR transporter: human LAT4 / SLC43A2, the ortholog of zebrafish slc43a2a (lat4a). The eight contacting residues are given with each panel species' residue at the aligned position, so that the flying-fish substitution can be tested against the site as soon as its position can be placed on a sequence (see slc43a2a_numbering_problem).

slc43a2a_numbering_problem.finding: The two slc43a2a positions our sources give -- F326L (the flying-fish convergent substitution, Daane 2021) and T200K (the zebrafish nr21 allele) -- do not match any fetched UniProt sequence of slc43a2a. In every zebrafish isoform (Q5PR35, A0ACD6B803, A0A8M1N3P6) residue 326 is D and residue 200 is M; in medaka (H2LJY1, H2LJX8) residue 326 is D and residue 200 is F. No single numbering offset in -60..+60 makes both stated wild-type residues appear at their stated positions in any of these sequences.
slc43a2a_numbering_problem.consequence: So the key structural question -- does the flying-fish convergent substitution sit in the substrate site? -- CANNOT be answered from fetched sources. Placing F326L on the LAT4 structure would require the sequence Daane 2021 numbered against, which is not in any record this layer fetched. Nothing is renumbered or guessed here.
slc43a2a_numbering_problem.RESOLVED: SOLVED, in structures/convergence-test.json. The numbering is against the ENSEMBL release 116 medaka protein, not the UniProt one. The sequence thread (sequences/alignments/slc43a2a.json) established this from Daane 2021 Data S1 sheet "G - conv. aa subst." and checked that the reference residue there is F. The site is human LAT4 position 320, 20.1 A from the bound substrate in 9JBT. The UniProt-based mapping in variant_positions_on_structures (position 300) is therefore WRONG; it is kept only to show what the error looked like before it was caught.
slc43a2a_numbering_problem.what_would_settle_it: the Lat4a reference sequence behind Figure 2 of PMID 34534441, or the authors' Data S1 alignment -- obtained by the sequence thread, see RESOLVED
slc43a2a_numbering_problem.incidental: Both zebrafish and medaka do carry a phenylalanine at position 340, 14 residues after the stated position. That is noted as a coincidence, not an identification.
